title: Doomsday pile ordering fails: GAME_TARGET IDs rejected despite being listed in choices
description:
During Doomsday pile construction, the LLM successfully selects 5 cards in phase 1 (choosing which cards go in the pile), but in phase 2 (ordering the pile), 3 of 4 IDs are consistently rejected with "Object pNN not found in current choices" even though those exact IDs appear in the choices list.

Evidence:
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260227_004918/Gem25P Lucky_pilot.log: 9 consecutive failures at pile ordering (lines 968-1073)
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260227_004918/Gem25P Lucky_mcp.log: auto-select and loop detection triggered (lines 371-382)
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260227_004918/Gem25P Lucky_errors.log: "Object p103/p78/p101 not found in current choices" (lines 15-23)
- Only p29 (Lotus Petal, already in graveyard) succeeded; p103 (Thassa's Oracle), p78 (Force of Will), p101 (Lion's Eye Diamond) all failed

Root cause: BridgeCallbackHandler.java:1176 stores target UUIDs in lastChoices, and BridgeCallbackHandler.java:1567-1570 compares the resolved UUID against lastChoices. Between choice presentation and LLM response, ShortIdRegistry mappings can change (via updateLastGameView or concurrent callbacks), causing resolve() to return a UUID that doesn't match what was stored in lastChoices. The Doomsday multi-step target sequence is especially vulnerable because cards move zones between selection phases, potentially getting new UUIDs while keeping the same short IDs.

Impact: Game-deciding. Gem25P Lucky could not construct its Doomsday pile, making the card completely unplayable. The bridge auto-selected random cards for the pile, and the game was effectively lost.

Suggested fix: Either (a) store short ID strings in lastChoices instead of UUIDs, so the comparison at line 1570 matches what the LLM sends directly, or (b) snapshot the shortId-to-UUID mappings at getActionChoices time and use the snapshot in chooseAction.
